note: The picker-free half of the work-scale measurement, and it needs no person: r2026-11-08-1080p-video's fixture and shape with the resize moved out of --size and into --work-scale 0.75. The client sends its frame at 2560x1440 and the rebuilt worker (patch f1908586c80c, r2026-11-10-3-ws-build, exit 0 with 17 shader modules - resize_rgba8 among them) resizes it to 1920x1080 inside the pass, runs the network there and resizes the published picture back to 2560x1440, so the capture chain does no videoscale at all. Read, in this order: the **median and steady rate against r2026-11-08-1080p-video's 27.4 ms / 36.5 fps** (1080p internal, resize done by gst's videoscale, capture 8.7 ms) and against **r2026-11-07-video-b's 35.2 ms / 28.4 fps** (1440p internal, no resize anywhere); then the **capture split's read against video-b's 6.4 ms**, because the pass does the resize now and the capture should be back at the no-scale figure. Then the artifact: `ws-video-after.png` must come back **2560x1440** - an after PNG at 1920x1080 means the upscale did not happen. How to read it: at ~27 ms with capture ~6.4 the resize has moved into the pass for nothing and the work-scale shape is the cheaper 1080p route; at ~35 ms the two dispatches over 11M pixels cost what gst's stage did, and the `--size 1920x1080` route stays the better one. Either landing is a reading, not a failure. Card gate applies as always: read gpu_before/gpu_after and idle_waited_s out of the report, and quote the spread beside the mean rather than a single number.
